scope: Compare libdxfrw's typed MLINESTYLE decode with independent LibreDWG minJSON for one physical AC1027 source profile, in addition to the already recorded frame identity, common links, ODA body rule, and dictionary membership.

implementation.method: The test adapter emits lossless text bytes as hex and typed scalar/element values from the real DWG decode. The verifier binds the source hash, requires the unique physical type-73/handle-0x18 peer object, compares strings and integer/color fields exactly, converts independent radians to degrees, compares floating fields with absolute tolerance 1e-12, verifies two ordered elements, and records the peer's exact 84-byte frame. Self-tests mutate angle, offset, and linetype index and require each mismatch to fail.

validation.verifierSelfTest: python3 tools/research/audit_ac1027_source_references.py --self-test: PASS; angle, offset, and linetype-index mutation rejection
validation.physicalAudit: audit_ac1027_source_references.py against hash-bound Cover.dwg and LibreDWG minJSON: PASS; source unchanged; 88/88 callback identities retained in the inventory (75 opaque frames, 13 standard objects); exact MLINESTYLE field differential passed

limitations: This is one hash-bound AC1027 producer/source profile; it does not establish other versions or producer prevalence.
LibreDWG minJSON exposes semantic values but not independent physical bit spans; exact per-field byte/bit boundaries and arbitrary trailing-byte accounting remain open.
The audit does not qualify MLINE entity geometry, native rendering, strict whole-document output, or broader MLINESTYLE writer support.
The source audit still observes strict conversion refusing the retained raw MLINESTYLE callback (qualified=4/5); no output support claim is promoted.
The generated mutation self-tests validate the comparator, not additional DWG fixtures or independent consumer behavior.
